release_notes: Postbacks that explain themselves. Common network status words now map out of the box: approved, confirmed, accepted and converted become sale, while declined, refused and cancelled become rejected - but only as the last resort before 'custom', so your own conversion types and {type}_status parameters always win. The campaign editor's S2S Postbacks tab gains a built-in postback tester: one click fires a real postback at your own server with a throwaway click, then shows a verdict for every stage - recording and status mapping, whether each S2S postback's statuses filter admits the conversion, a live probe delivery with HTTP code and timing, unresolved macros such as {external_id} or {sub_id_N} that would ship to the source as literal text (Keitaro's own #1 FAQ failure), and whether the queue worker is alive - then cleans up after itself, leaving only an audit line in the incoming log. The in-panel update now self-heals: a missing queue-worker cron is installed automatically after updating, and a worker that has not pinged recently reports its last error right in the update output; the cron's log path is unified to var/logs. Runs on PHP 8.1-8.5 (v1.5.10 fixed the PHP < 8.4 postback regression).
